title: FortiSandbox Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Access Sensitive Information via Crafted HTTP Requests
content_md: Fortinet has disclosed a high-severity vulnerability in its FortiSandbox product line that could allow unauthenticated attackers to access sensitive information by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the platform’s web interface. Tracked as CVE-2026-26084, the flaw affects FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS deployments. Fortinet assigned the issue a CVSS v3.1 score of 8.9, reflecting the potential impact of an attacker accessing operational data without valid credentials, user interaction, or prior privileges. FortiSandbox Flaw According to Fortinet’s security advisory , CVE-2026-26084 is an improper access control vulnerability classified as CWE-284. The weakness exists in a graphical user interface component shared across affected FortiSandbox deployments. In practice, the issue means the FortiSandbox web interface may not adequately validate whether an HTTP request originates from an authenticated, authorized session before exposing protected information. An attacker familiar with the application’s internal API structure could send crafted requests directly to vulnerable endpoints and potentially bypass normal authentication controls. The vulnerability has a network-based attack vector and requires no user interaction, making internet-exposed or insufficiently segmented management interfaces a particular concern.
